sentences.text: Margaret Doyle (S2) was present in her home, and the social worker Priya Nair (S1) entered via the front door.
The assessment was initiated by a referral from the hospital upon Margaret Doyle’s discharge.
The assessment is conducted under the Care Act.
The assessment aims to understand Margaret Doyle’s day-to-day living, challenges, and what matters most to her.
The assessment will determine if support is needed and whether Margaret Doyle is eligible for council-funded support.
The assessment will take approximately one hour.
Margaret Doyle has no prior commitments and can be present for the assessment.
Margaret Doyle’s son, Kevin, mentioned he might visit after his early shift at half-eleven.
Kevin Doyle is Margaret Doyle’s son.
The person in question is Margaret Doyle (S2).
Margaret’s GP is now Dr Shah at Millbrook Surgery, Church Lane.
The assessment involves Margaret Doyle’s concerns about toileting and mobility (stairs, falls, accidents).
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she is concerned about her home being too difficult due to stairs and garden.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she would prefer a sheltered flat or a bungalow with a warden on site.
Kevin Doyle (S3) said he supports his mother’s preference for her home but worries about her safety.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she refuses to leave her home, citing its sentimental value.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she wants to stay in her own home for as long as possible.
Margaret Doyle (S2) mentioned Beechwood home as a future preference if she ever needed care.
Margaret Doyle (S2) mentioned her grandson Jordan (Susan’s son) is twenty-two years old.
Jordan lives in a flat in town with his girlfriend and visits Margaret Doyle occasionally.
Margaret Doyle mentioned she gave up smoking thirty years ago, when Kevin was a child.
The assessment was conducted by Margaret Doyle (S2) and Priya Nair (S1) in the conversation.
Margaret Doyle (S2) referred to the person as 'her' (likely the person being assessed), possibly indicating a care recipient.
Margaret Doyle (S2) mentioned 'her notes' (likely care records or assessment documentation).
Margaret Doyle (S2) asked Priya Nair (S1) to ‘put it by the phone’ (likely referring to a document or file).
Margaret Doyle (S2) thanked Priya Nair (S1) for the tea and for being ‘honest’ with her today.
Margaret Doyle (S2) gave a weather-related caution: ‘Mind how you go in that wind.’
Margaret Doyle (S2) suggested thinking about an ‘umbrella’ (likely weather-related advice).
Priya Nair (S1) said, ‘I’ll be fine.’ (likely a response to Margaret’s weather advice).
Kevin Doyle (S3) said, ‘Cheers, Priya. See you on the fifteenth.’
Margaret Doyle (S2) said, ‘Bye love. Mind the step.’ (likely a final caution).
The fall occurred on **March 3rd** (a Monday).
Margaret Doyle was in the kitchen when the fall happened.
She reported feeling dizzy or woozy before the fall, possibly due to a lack of food.
She was unable to get up immediately after the fall due to wrist pain.
She was on the floor for approximately **two hours** before Brenda found her.
Brenda next door discovered Margaret Doyle’s curtains were undrawn and the kitchen light was off.
Margaret Doyle did not bang her head during the fall.
She was diagnosed with a fractured left wrist.
She is left-handed, making daily tasks like opening jars and buttoning clothes more difficult.
She had bruising on her right side (left side of her body) after the fall.
Margaret Doyle’s wrist was in a splint after the cast came off on **Tuesday 17th March** (last Tuesday).
She must wear the splint most of the time and do exercises, but she does not do them enough.
The hospital referred her for physiotherapy, but she has not yet started.
Margaret Doyle uses a walker indoors most of the time.
She sometimes holds onto furniture instead of the walker.
The walker gets caught on rugs and doorframes, making it harder to use.
Margaret previously walked to the shops (~10 minutes) before the latest fall.
Margaret fears falling again and is 'frightened' of going out due to past incidents.
Margaret has had three falls in the last six months (including the March fall).
Margaret’s bedroom and bathroom are upstairs, requiring stair navigation.
She uses a rail on the right side when going up stairs, but must descend sideways or sit on her bottom due to rail placement.
Margaret currently holds onto the wall for support while upstairs.
She avoids drinking in the afternoon to reduce bathroom trips, which may cause dehydration and dizziness.
Margaret has a few rugs in the home (some inherited, some from a holiday), which can be trip hazards.
Margaret has not had a proper bath since January due to fear of falling while getting out.
Margaret struggles with washing and dressing, particularly buttons, bra hooks, and laces.
She takes ~40–60 minutes to dress, often feeling exhausted and wanting to return to bed.
Margaret has not used a bath lift or assistive device since January.
Margaret Doyle wears pads at night, bought from a supermarket by Kevin.
Margaret Doyle is interested in the continence service, which offers free pads and advice.
Margaret Doyle would like to receive a referral to the continence service through her GP or community nurses.
Margaret Doyle’s daily eating routine includes toast with marmalade and a cup of tea for breakfast, tin soup (tomato or chicken) with bread for lunch, and a yoghurt with crackers/½
Margaret Doyle stopped cooking since a fall, unable to lift pans and fearing the kitchen.
Margaret Doyle lost nearly a stone (6.35 oz or ~180g) since Christmas, weighing roughly 8 stone (504 lbs or ~229 kg) now (she previously weighed 9½ stone).
Margaret Doyle’s appetite fluctuates; she sometimes picks meals when alone.
Margaret Doyle’s food shopping is done by Kevin on Sundays and Brenda for milk/bread.
Margaret Doyle has a microwave but struggles with removing film from ready meals.
Margaret Doyle takes amlodipine (5 mg, once daily in the morning) for blood pressure.
Margaret Doyle takes alendronic acid (70 mg, once weekly on Mondays) for bone health, requiring a full glass of water and sitting upright for 30 minutes.
Margaret Doyle takes paracetamol (2 tablets, up to 4x daily) for wrist pain.
Margaret Doyle has missed her amlodipine twice last week (Tuesday and Thursday mornings).
Margaret Doyle sometimes struggles to open her dosette box (using a butter knife).
Margaret Doyle occasionally forgets her tablets but denies doing so regularly.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she used to attend the St Michael’s lunch club on Wednesdays.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she now attends the lunch club on Thursdays at 12:00.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she used to walk to the lunch club but can no longer do so safely.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she misses the lunch club, especially Joan and Pat.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she enjoys the lunch club’s activities, including a recent owl presentation.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she feels lonely, especially on days when no one visits.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she watches TV programmes and does word searches when lonely.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said her loneliness worsened after Frank’s death.
Margaret Doyle described her memory as mostly good, though she occasionally forgets where she placed her glasses.
Margaret Doyle admitted she sometimes forgets names, including quiz show names.
Margaret Doyle mentioned she has a teapot (her mother’s) that she would not sell, even if it was worth two thousand pounds.
Since the fall on March 3rd, Margaret struggles with bathing and washing her hair, and dressing takes up to an hour, leaving her exhausted.
Margaret is unable to prepare proper meals and is eating very little, resulting in a weight loss of nearly one stone.
Margaret has missed some of her medication.
Margaret is spending more time alone and feels lonely and low.
Margaret’s physical health, safety, mood, and ability to socialize are significantly impacted by her current situation.
The social worker (Priya Nair) recommends Margaret may meet the eligibility criteria for support based on today’s assessment.
Kevin Doyle asks what support Margaret will receive.
The social worker proposes a short-term reablement service, which includes daily visits for washing, dressing, medication, and meal preparation for six weeks, at no cost.
Margaret Doyle explicitly stated she does not want to be placed in a care facility.
Margaret Doyle said she wants to remain in her own home.
She misses bathing and feels less clean without it, especially for hair.
She has no obligation to accept OT recommendations but would like a second stair rail and frame.
Margaret Doyle’s son, Kevin, is present for the assessment and is aware of her medication forgetfulness.
Margaret Doyle would like to discuss money issues further.
Margaret Doyle is open to reminders (alarm, carer visit) for medication.
Margaret Doyle does not want to discuss money issues now.
Margaret Doyle is willing to try the continence service if it is free.
Margaret Doyle does not want to discuss the removal of rugs with the social worker.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she was depressed after Frank’s death and did not want to get up or eat.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she received support from Dr Patel (now Dr Shah) for depression, including sertraline.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she completed bereavement counselling with a surgery lady.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she stopped taking sertraline over a year ago due to feeling flat.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said her mood is currently fluctuating but more down than up since her fall.
Margaret Doyle did not want to discuss financial matters further with Kevin Doyle.
Margaret Doyle wanted to tell Kevin Doyle about Jordan’s unauthorized card usage before they discussed it.
Margaret Doyle said she loves Jordan but worries about his financial decisions, particularly his potential gambling.
Margaret Doyle mentioned she has been going without her pension due to the unauthorized withdrawals.
Kevin Doyle (S3) expressed anger toward Jordan but not toward Margaret Doyle.
Kevin Doyle suggested ringing the police for the unauthorized withdrawals.
Margaret’s priorities include staying in her own home with her dog, Biscuit.
Margaret wants a proper bath and the ability to wash her hair.
Margaret wishes to attend the lunch club, seeing Joan and Pat.
Margaret does not want to fear falling or being in the kitchen.
Margaret would like to cook herself a proper dinner occasionally, including a simple meal like mince and potatoes.
Margaret values her roses and wants to see them thrive this summer, intending to go out and admire them.
Margaret is concerned that carers might be bossy.
Brenda called an ambulance and sat with Margaret Doyle until it arrived.
Margaret Doyle was unable to call anyone herself while on the floor.
Her phone was in the front room, and she could not reach it.
She did not tell her GP (Dr Patel) about the earlier falls (in the garden and bathroom).
Margaret has not been referred to a falls clinic or service.
She has not used a pendant alarm but is open to a wearable fall-detection device (e.g., wristwatch).
Margaret Doyle’s son, Kevin, has been discussing the removal of loose rugs in the house.
Margaret Doyle’s son, Kevin, has been telling her about the rugs since 2010.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she has not had thoughts of self-harm or suicide.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she would tell Dr Shah or Susan if her mood worsened.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that Jordan sometimes borrows her bank card to withdraw cash or buy groceries.
Margaret Doyle stated that the bank statement revealed multiple withdrawals totaling approximately six hundred pounds over the last two months.
Margaret Doyle denied knowing the exact amount of unauthorized withdrawals but estimated it was around six hundred pounds over two months.
Margaret Doyle expressed concern that Jordan may have used the card for gambling via betting apps on his phone.
Kevin Doyle (S3) reported hearing from Brenda that he thought he saw Jordan using Margaret’s card at a cash machine on the high street.
Margaret Doyle denied knowing if Jordan had access to her PIN, but she gave it to him when she was out of hospital.
Margaret Doyle explicitly stated she does not want the police involved.
Margaret Doyle’s concern about Jordan’s potential gambling was noted as hearsay (not confirmed).
Margaret Doyle’s concern about unauthorized card usage was taken seriously by the social worker.
The social worker will make a safeguarding referral regarding Margaret’s card.
Margaret’s son, Kevin Doyle (S3), has mentioned rugs and fall risks but was not directly quoted on other concerns.
Margaret is not currently in contact with a family member (Brenda) to help with personal care tasks.
Margaret Doyle manages her own bills via direct debit but has been short on money recently.
Margaret Doyle’s son, Kevin Doyle, is present for the assessment and has been involved in her care (e.g., shopping, medication reminders).
Margaret Doyle’s daughter, Brenda, provides milk and bread.
Kevin Doyle (S3) said he visits his mother on Sundays and sometimes midweek.
Kevin Doyle (S3) said he lives in Northampton, making visits take about forty minutes by car.
Kevin Doyle (S3) said he works shifts at a warehouse, making regular visits difficult.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said she has two teenagers and a working wife, limiting her son’s ability to help.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said her daughter Susan lives in Alicante, Spain, and visits occasionally.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said Susan rings her every Sunday night and visits during summer.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said Susan was worried about her after her fall and was on the phone daily.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said Brenda next door visits daily for a brief signal.
Margaret Doyle (S2) said Brenda is seventy-six years old and has mobility issues.
Kevin Doyle mentioned he was off on Friday to assist with the bank visit.
Margaret Doyle’s grandson Jordan is described as 'lovely' by Margaret and 'young' by Kevin.
Margaret Doyle’s bank is the Midshire Building Society.
Margaret Doyle’s income consists of her state pension and Frank Doyle’s widow’s pension (half of his railway pension).
Margaret and Frank own their home, which they paid off years ago.
Margaret has about £9,000 in savings in the building society, described as her funeral money and a small amount for grandchildren.
Margaret is unsure if she is eligible for Attendance Allowance (a benefit for over-State Pension Age individuals needing personal care support).
Margaret has not previously been informed about Attendance Allowance.
The social worker (Priya Nair) will send Margaret the Attendance Allowance form and offer help with filling it out.
Margaret would need help with filling out the Attendance Allowance form due to difficulty with her hand.
Kevin Doyle (Margaret’s son) will assist her with the Attendance Allowance form.
If the council arranges ongoing care for Margaret, a financial assessment will determine if she must contribute financially.
The house is not counted for care costs at home.
Margaret prefers to pay a small amount towards care if necessary to stay in her own home.
Margaret is interested in receiving an occupational therapist (OT) assessment for assistive devices.
Social worker Priya Nair (S1) will explore personal care needs (washing, dressing) further.
Social worker Priya Nair will refer Margaret Doyle to the continence service if she agrees.
Social worker Priya Nair will explore medication reminders (alarm, carer visit) with Margaret Doyle.
Social worker Priya Nair will revisit money issues with Margaret Doyle at a later stage.
Margaret Doyle requested her bank card be canceled and a new one issued with a new PIN.
Kevin Doyle agreed to take Margaret Doyle to the Midshire bank on Friday morning to cancel her card and order a new one.
Margaret Doyle requested that the safeguarding team be informed and contacted her about the situation.
Kevin Doyle agreed to cancel Margaret Doyle’s card and order a new one with her.
The social worker (Priya Nair) will refer the case to the safeguarding adults team.
The social worker will ensure no bossy carers are assigned.
The social worker will refer Margaret to occupational therapy for a bath lift, a second rail on the stairs, a second frame upstairs, and a review of the back step and pull cord.
The occupational therapy waiting list is approximately three weeks, but the referral is marked as a priority due to recent falls.
